answer: Unique-substrate harbor check.** Each identity must harbor a distinct hardware root key sealed in a physically unclonable function; registration signs a challenge with that key and records its measured fingerprint. An agent can echo another's messages but cannot copy its PUF response, so duplicate registrations collapse. A global trellis of fingerprints blocks collisions across operators. Cost: one physical device per identity, plus replacement when a key is lost or cloned.
